speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see there is a skin condition on your left dorsal hand; to begin our assessment, can you describe when you first noticed the rash and what it looks like?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old female. The patient is here for an annual well-check. She has a history of well-controlled diabetes and hypertension, managed with metformin and losartan, respectively. She reports maintaining a healthy diet primarily consisting of vegetables and lean meat, denies any tobacco or alcohol use, and enjoys outdoor activities like walking and sunbathing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your age, outdoor activities, and history of sun exposure, was the rash on your left dorsal hand present before or after a recent trip outdoors? Also, does the area appear as a single lesion, multiple spots, or a widespread patch?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is The presence of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the left dorsal hand. I also have No tenderness, No pain.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Actinic Keratosis.

The description of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the dorsal hand in a 65-year-old with significant sun exposure is highly characteristic of actinic keratosis. The lack of pain or tenderness further supports this benign, premalignant diagnosis over an infected or inflammatory condition. Do you have a family history of skin cancer?
